name: Null-Trace Signal Mortuary Kit
description:
The Null-Trace Signal Mortuary Kit is a portable electronic warfare package produced under a civilian security consulting label by Ringo Corponation, designed to excise an operator's electromagnetic presence from a local environment. The kit consists of three primary components: a broadband passive absorber vest that intercepts and grounds outgoing RF emissions from any devices on the wearer's person, a localized mesh jammer module the size of a flask that suppresses active scanning signals in a 4-meter radius without producing a detectable jamming signature, and a spoofing beacon the size of a coin that can be placed separately to broadcast a fabricated 'ghost signal' — an idle, plausible device signature that draws automated sweep attention away from the operator.

The mesh jammer's 'silent jamming' architecture is the kit's most technically notable feature. Standard jammers suppress signals by flooding the frequency band with noise, which is itself trivially detectable. The Mortuary's jammer instead exploits a vulnerability in the handshake protocols used by most commercial and mid-tier corporate scanning infrastructure, inserting a spoofed 'clear scan' response that satisfies the sweep query without revealing the jammer's presence. Against hardened military-grade scanning the technique fails, but hardened military-grade scanning is not what most operators encounter in GLMZ's commercial and corporate spaces.

The kit takes its name from its operational philosophy, a phrase that circulates in professional circles: 'you want to be a dead signal, not a hidden one — hidden things get looked for.' The distinction is meaningful. A gap in a signal environment draws attention; a plausible, boring signal does not.

specifications.passive_absorption_efficiency: 97% for signals below 6 GHz, 84% for 6-40 GHz range
specifications.jammer_detection_signature: Undetectable to Tier 1-2 sweep systems; flagged by Tier 3+ dedicated sniffers
specifications.ghost_beacon_duration: Up to 72 hours on internal cell
specifications.kit_weight: 1.4 kg total (vest 0.9 kg, jammer 0.3 kg, beacon 0.2 kg)
specifications.failure_mode: Vest absorption saturates under simultaneous multi-band active scanning; jammer exploit patched in some post-2187 infrastructure
specifications.form_factor: Three-component kit, packable to messenger bag size

tactical_use: Deployed before entry to a monitored area: operator dons the vest, activates the jammer module, and places the ghost beacon at a distance to anchor surveillance attention to a fixed false positive. Effective for sustained operations in corporate lobbies, transit infrastructure, and mid-security facilities. The jammer's infrastructure-exploit vulnerability to post-2187 security updates is a known liability — experienced operators sweep their target environment first to assess what scanning generation they're working against before committing to the Mortuary as primary coverage.
cultural_context: The Mortuary Kit has a reputation for being the professional's tool — not glamorous, not visually impressive, but reliable and thoughtfully designed. Operators who use it tend to be methodical, patient types who plan their approaches carefully. In contrast to the aspirational cachet of something like a thermoptic shroud, the Mortuary signals competence over flash. Ringo Corponation sells it under a consulting-security license that technically requires corporate or law-enforcement affiliation to purchase, a requirement that is honored primarily in the breach.
known_users: mid-tier fixers with methodical operational styles
story_hooks: A ghost beacon from a Mortuary Kit is found still broadcasting in a location where a prominent figure died three weeks ago — officially ruled an accident. Someone was running a professional signal operation that night.

Ringo Corponation's jammer exploit has been quietly patched in a specific district's scanning infrastructure, apparently in response to a recent high-profile breach. Every operator who relied on the kit in that zone is now running blind and doesn't know it.

A player is hired to find someone who has completely vanished from GLMZ's signal environment — no ghost beacon, no RF footprint, nothing. Either they're dead or they have something better than a Mortuary Kit. The client needs to know which.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions GhostNet EW-4 Electronic Warfare

physical_description.visual_profile: A tactical stealth kit comprising three distinct components: a form-fitting body garment embedded with conductive mesh, a small cylindrical module resembling a military-grade flask, and a coin-sized disc. The ensemble presents as professional security equipment rather than improvised hardware — industrial-grade but deliberately unmarked.
physical_description.dimensions: Vest fits standard torso; jammer module 12cm height × 6cm diameter; beacon coin 3cm diameter × 0.8cm thickness. Full kit compresses to roughly 35cm × 25cm × 10cm when packed.
physical_description.weight_description: Light enough for all-day wear — 1.4 kg distributed across three pieces. Vest adds negligible burden under clothing; jammer and beacon are pocket-portable.
physical_description.primary_material: Vest: woven carbon-fiber mesh over moisture-wicking synthetic backing. Jammer module: anodized aluminum chassis with embedded ferrite cores. Beacon: composite polymer shell with internal cellular battery.
physical_description.finish: Vest surface is matte-black with subtle RF-absorbing texture (reminiscent of anechoic chamber material). Jammer module shows industrial finish with faint machine marks; beacon is unmarked matte-gray polymer.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic — blacks, dark grays, anodized silver accents. No branding colors visible. Deliberately dull.
physical_description.interface_elements: Vest: internal contact points for jammer module dock (magnetic quick-release). Jammer: single recessed power button, tri-color LED indicator (amber/green/red), micro USB charging port. Beacon: external activation dial (12-position setting ring for device profile selection), micro-contact charging pads on base.
distinctive_features: Jammer module's tri-LED status ring: amber indicates standby, green = silent suppression active, red = saturation warning
Beacon's mechanical profile-selector dial with barely-visible numerical index (1-12), requiring tactile memory or external reference
Vest's internal conductive weave visible at seams and neckline — suggests technical sophistication to trained observers
Absence of any manufacturer branding on visible surfaces (RINGO markings appear only on warranty card inside packaging)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: RINGO CORPORATION subdued laser-etched on inner vest panel and jammer module base (easily obscured). Regulatory stamps on jammer appear generic (intentionally vague compliance labeling). Beacon unmarked.
physical_description.condition_typical: In use: vest worn under tactical jacket or oversized hoodie; jammer module clipped to waistband or secured in chest rig; beacon deployed on window ledge, roof access, or dead drop location several meters from operator. Equipment shows minor cosmetic wear (scuff marks on jammer, fabric pilling on vest seams) consistent with repeated deployment.
